title: New York's 21st Congressional District Election, 2026
description: New York's 21st Congressional District is an open seat covering 15 counties across the North Country and Mohawk Valley, a deeply red district. Incumbent Republican Elise Stefanik, first elected in 2014, declined to seek re-election after ending her brief gubernatorial bid, triggering competitive primaries in both parties. The Democratic primary features dairy farmer Blake Gendebien against Lake Placid restaurateur Stuart Amoriell, while the Republican primary pits state Assemblyman Robert Smullen, who has institutional party backing, against Sticker Mule CEO Anthony Constantino, who has Donald Trump's endorsement and is self-funding his campaign. The winner of the June 23 primary will advance to the general election in a district that last elected a Democrat in 2009.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race at the time of research.

candidates.name: Blake Gendebien
candidates.summary: Blake Gendebien is a second-generation dairy farmer and co-owner of Twin Mill Farms in Lisbon, New York. He emphasizes lowering costs, protecting rural healthcare access, securing the border, and representing the North Country in Washington. He previously served as Vice Chair of the Cooperative Board of Agri-Mark and co-founded the Jules of Life Foundation to help families navigate pediatric cancer care.

candidates.name: Stuart Amoriell
candidates.summary: Stuart Amoriell is a Lake Placid restaurant owner and business owner running as an 'independent Democrat' with a grassroots campaign. His platform focuses on affordable and accessible healthcare through Medicare for All, affordable housing and childcare, lowering the cost of living, and a just and compassionate immigration policy. He advocates for rebuilding rural communities and strengthening economic fairness for working families.

candidates.name: Anthony Constantino
candidates.summary: Anthony Constantino is the CEO and founder of Sticker Mule, a global online printing company headquartered in Amsterdam, New York. A political newcomer endorsed by President Donald Trump, he is self-funding his campaign and emphasizes job creation, American manufacturing, border security, and cutting government regulations. He holds a degree in economics from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and has promoted automation and patriotic themes throughout his campaign.

candidates.name: Robert Smullen
candidates.summary: Robert Smullen is a New York State Assemblyman representing the 118th district since 2019, encompassing parts of the North Country and Mohawk Valley. A 24-year U.S. Marine Corps veteran retiring as a colonel and a former White House Fellow, he focuses on federal energy policy, northern border security, rural healthcare access, and veterans' issues. He has the backing of the state Republican and Conservative parties and holds multiple master's degrees from institutions including Georgetown University and the National Defense University.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, so the forecast relies entirely on district fundamentals. NY-21 is described as a deeply red district spanning 15 counties in the North Country and Mohawk Valley. Republicans have held this seat continuously since 2009 (when a Democrat last won it). The open-seat dynamic created by Stefanik's departure introduces some uncertainty, but the district's strong Republican lean means the eventual GOP nominee — whether institutional candidate Smullen or Trump-endorsed/self-funded Constantino — will be heavily favored in the general election. Democrats are running a contested primary as well, but no Democrat has won here in 17 years. The June 23 primary is just days away, but without any public polling of either primary or general matchups, confidence remains medium and the rating stays at likely_r rather than safe_r.
